roster.full_name: Together (B'Yachad) - alliance of Bennett 2026 and Yesh Atid
Religious Zionist Party - Zehut (technical/joint list arrangement)
Blue and White (Benny Gantz's remnant list)

components: independents / technocratic list led by Eisenkot (incl. Hili Tropper, Elazar Stern)

roster.full_name: The Reservists - New Economic Party alliance

components: new list founded by Ofer Winter
grassroots Haredi movement that failed to get list slots from Shas/UTJ, then ran independently

stances.speaker: Benny Gantz
stances.quote: Netanyahu should not continue as prime minister, and I will not give him his 61st vote.
stances.paraphrase: Gantz pledged he will not provide Netanyahu the decisive 61st Knesset seat needed to form a government.

stances.speaker: Naftali Bennett
stances.quote: I will not allow that failed and divisive leadership to continue, nor will I be part of it.
stances.paraphrase: Bennett said he would not join or allow a continuation of Netanyahu's leadership, before Together was formally launched.

stances.speaker: Avigdor Liberman
stances.quote: even if the world turns upside down
stances.paraphrase: Liberman said he would not serve under Netanyahu under any circumstances, open to a Likud-led government only without Netanyahu.

stances.speaker: Gadi Eisenkot
stances.quote: not fit to hold any leadership position
stances.paraphrase: Eisenkot said Netanyahu and his security cabinet are unfit for any leadership role, ruling him out as a partner.

stances.speaker: Likud party (official statement)
stances.quote: There is no room in the Knesset for those who harm IDF soldiers and are unable to say that Hamas and Hezbollah are terrorist organizations
stances.paraphrase: Likud announced it will petition the Central Elections Committee to disqualify Ra'am and the Joint List from the election.

stances.speaker: Avigdor Liberman / party platform
stances.quote: anti-Zionist
stances.paraphrase: Yisrael Beiteinu's platform rejects joining a coalition with Arab parties, calling such a move anti-Zionist, despite having relied on Ra'am's support while in the Bennett-Lapid government.

stances.speaker: Reservists-NEP platform (as characterized by Wikipedia editors)
stances.quote: Zionist unity government
stances.paraphrase: The Reservists-NEP alliance advocates a 'Zionist unity government' that would exclude both Arab and Haredi parties; this is a characterization of the platform, not a verified direct quote from Hendel or Zelekha.

stances.condition: if Ra'am's votes are needed to topple the Netanyahu government
stances.speaker: Yair Golan
stances.quote: If we must rely on the votes of the Ra'am party to topple this failed government of disaster... then Ra'am is a worthy partner.
stances.paraphrase: Golan said he would accept relying on Ra'am's votes to remove the Netanyahu government, urging fellow opposition leaders to do the same.

stances.speaker: Yousef Jabareen
stances.quote: removing Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir, and Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich from power
stances.paraphrase: The Joint List states removing Netanyahu, Ben-Gvir and Smotrich from power is a central electoral objective, while not committing to any particular Jewish-led coalition.

stances.condition: depends on coalition negotiations and who is building the government
stances.speaker: Mansour Abbas (characterized)
stances.quote: would not rule out potential coalition partners
stances.paraphrase: Abbas has refused to commit to either the political Left or Right and is leaving room to negotiate with any side that can build a government.

stances.speaker: Yair Golan
stances.quote: the Haredim will be outside [the government], that is a guarantee.
stances.paraphrase: After a leaked clip suggested openness to Haredi partners, Golan publicly reversed and guaranteed Haredi parties would be excluded from a Democrats-backed government.

stances.condition: everyone must commit to universal enlistment with no exemptions
stances.speaker: Oded Forer (MK, Yisrael Beiteinu)
stances.quote: anyone who wants to be a partner in the next government must commit: enlistment for everyone, no exemptions.
stances.paraphrase: Yisrael Beiteinu conditioned coalition partnership on universal draft enlistment, which effectively excludes Shas and UTJ as currently positioned.

stances.condition: passage of legislation shielding Haredi draft-evaders from enforcement
stances.speaker: Aryeh Deri
stances.quote: without the passage of two laws to defend draft dodgers, there was nothing to talk about
stances.paraphrase: Deri said Shas would not commit to post-election loyalty to Netanyahu's bloc until draft-shielding legislation passes first.

stances.speaker: Moshe Gafni
stances.quote: as of now, there is no bloc
stances.paraphrase: Gafni declined to commit UTJ to the Netanyahu bloc in advance, saying no bloc commitment exists until conditions are met.

stances.speaker: Rabbi Yitzhak Yosef (Shas spiritual leader, as characterized by reporting)
stances.quote: signals possible opening to rival Gadi Eisenkot
stances.paraphrase: Journalists reported that Shas's spiritual leader appeared to open the door to a future Eisenkot-led government while criticizing Netanyahu; this is a media characterization, not a direct Shas pledge.

stances.condition: Shas must accept Eisenkot's three principles: Israel as a Jewish and democratic state, Declaration of Independence values, and universal national service
stances.speaker: Gadi Eisenkot
stances.quote: I see Shas as a partner on the condition that it accepts the three foundational principles.
stances.paraphrase: Eisenkot said he would partner with Shas only if it accepts his three foundational principles, including universal national service.

stances.condition: Golan said he would accept a Haredi partner only if Likud, Smotrich and Ben Gvir were not in the government
stances.speaker: Yair Golan
stances.quote: provided that Likud, Smotrich, and Ben Gvir are not there
stances.paraphrase: Golan indicated any government he would support must exclude Likud, Smotrich (RZP), and Ben Gvir (Otzma).

stances.condition: Golan said he would accept a Haredi partner only if Likud, Smotrich and Ben Gvir were not in the government
stances.speaker: Yair Golan
stances.quote: provided that Likud, Smotrich, and Ben Gvir are not there
stances.paraphrase: Golan indicated any government he would support must exclude Likud, Smotrich (RZP), and Ben Gvir (Otzma).

stances.speaker: Otzma Yehudit (party statement)
stances.quote: there will be no talks, or meetings, or discussions on the topic, not directly, and not indirectly.
stances.paraphrase: Ben-Gvir's Otzma Yehudit rejected Netanyahu's demand to merge with Smotrich's Religious Zionist Party, ruling out any merger talks.

stances.condition: unconfirmed - based on unnamed sources close to Ben-Gvir
stances.speaker: unnamed sources close to Itamar Ben-Gvir
stances.quote: Netanyahu has already made a preliminary decision to try to form a broad national government, even at the cost of leaving Ben-Gvir outside.
stances.paraphrase: Sources close to Ben-Gvir claim Netanyahu may be preparing to pursue a broad national government that would leave Otzma Yehudit out, though this is unconfirmed by Netanyahu or Likud directly.

stances.speaker: Yashar / Democrats (joint announcement)
stances.quote: every ballot cast by Israelis seeking change
stances.paraphrase: Yashar and the Democrats signed a surplus-vote sharing agreement to maximize the opposition change bloc's Knesset seats.

stances.speaker: Yisrael Beiteinu / Together (joint announcement)
stances.quote: the loss of votes
stances.paraphrase: Yisrael Beiteinu and Together (B'Yachad) signed a surplus-vote sharing agreement, part of a wave of opposition pacts aimed at preventing wasted votes.

stances.speaker: Ra'am / Joint List
stances.quote: surplus-vote agreement
stances.paraphrase: Ra'am and the Joint List signed a surplus-vote agreement despite an earlier collapse of talks over a full electoral merger.

stances.speaker: Ofer Winter
stances.quote: I don't work for Netanyahu. I don't work for anyone.
stances.paraphrase: Winter positioned Amcha Yisrael as independent of Netanyahu, aiming to be a pivotal partner that pushes policy demands from within any right-leaning coalition rather than ruling Netanyahu out.

stances.speaker: Benny Gantz
stances.quote: Israel requires fresh leadership and a broader coalition rather than another narrow government dependent on extremist parties
stances.paraphrase: Gantz said Israel needs a broad coalition rather than another narrow government dependent on the current far-right/Haredi coalition partners.

gaps: No verbatim, directly-attributed quote was found for Yoaz Hendel or Yaron Zelekha personally on excluding Arab or Haredi parties; the 'Zionist unity government' characterization comes from a Wikipedia summary of the party's platform, not a quote captured from a news article.

Exact publication dates for the Jerusalem Post 'Israel Election 2026' explainer articles on Ra'am/Joint List (article-907154) and Shas/UTJ (article-907982) could not be confirmed; dates used in the stances table for these sources are estimated from surrounding article-ID sequencing and should be treated as approximate.

The Ra'am-Joint List surplus-vote pact date (2026-09-01) is inferred from the Wikipedia election article's ordering of events, not a specific dated news report; a primary news article confirming the exact signing date was not fetched.
Blue & White's current full platform and whether Gantz is running as a prime ministerial candidate versus a coalition partner was not conclusively established; pm_candidate is left null.

Haredi Public's Sephardi/Ashkenazi composition and its precise relationship to Shas and UTJ voters (whether it will pull more from one than the other) is not established; classified as family 'other' rather than one of the two Haredi families.
Amcha Yisrael's precise ideological family (religious-zionist vs. far-right vs. other) is ambiguous in sourcing; classified as 'other' pending clearer characterization.

No direct sourced statement was found of Likud or the Netanyahu bloc explicitly and formally excluding Yisrael Beiteinu or Blue & White (as opposed to the reverse); only the reverse direction (opposition parties excluding Netanyahu) was well sourced.

Could not source a statement from UTJ or Shas specifically naming Yisrael Beiteinu or the Democrats as unacceptable partners, only the general condition that draft-shielding legislation must pass first.

The claim that Netanyahu may be willing to leave Ben-Gvir/Otzma out of a future 'broad national government' rests entirely on unnamed sources 'close to Ben-Gvir' as reported by Jerusalem Post (2026-09-13); it is not confirmed by Netanyahu, Likud, or Ben-Gvir directly and should be treated as speculative.
Otzma Yehudit's own stance toward the Arab lists or toward a Netanyahu-led broad coalition was not directly sourced with a verbatim quote from Ben-Gvir himself in this research pass.
